title: St. Anky
imageAlt: St. Anky, a small dark-skinned gnome in a green hood and cloak, raising a wooden tankard
imageCaption: St. Anky — adventurer, traveler, and remembered ally.
dek: A traveler and sharing knight who carries uncertainty, humor and practical care into the institutions he leaves behind.

facts.Voraketh role: Early chronicler and Temple of Secrets founder/co-founder
facts.Death: 20 Apr 2026 · killed by a construct at the Binding Chains

body:
Anky’s record crosses ancient history, divine service, peace-making, the Shadow Roads, and Voraketh. The island provides the clearest longitudinal history: a frightened and disordered mind becomes one of the community’s strongest builders of memory.

Witness to the Gate’s construction

On 30 December 2024, St. Anky travels with Olokun, Cecil, Coralyn, and Fenwick into ancient Prima. They encounter young Papirus, Cala, and Nuru while the Gate is being built and choose to contribute information—a map of the shattered world—rather than rewrite the catastrophe outright.

Nuru’s mad saint

On 30 May 2025, Nuru addresses Anky as a “trembling vessel of shattered thought,” recognizes an intact shard of reason beneath his disorder, calls him “O mad saint,” and grants him the powers of a death cleric. Nuru also says the gods are fighting and losing while using their remaining strength to stave off “the end......of all things.”

During the 24 June peace negotiation with Ephraith, Anky identifies himself as Nuru’s holy saint and cupbearer, offers to bear burdens, and proposes peace through mutual respect and acknowledged boundaries. Nuru manifests and publicly declares: “MY CUPBEARER HAS SPOKEN!” The later phrase “Nuru... me pal....” therefore rests on an observed relationship, not merely imagined intimacy.

The Shadow Roads

Anky is present when the party enters the Shadow Roads on 14 September 2025. His precise actions during the crossing remain unrecovered, but the event places him among the travelers repeatedly entering dangerous systems without complete knowledge.

Voraketh takes something

Before 5 March 2026, Anky had already entered Voraketh’s Wasteland and lost something important. He said Stinky had gone silent and believed the Maw could suck things out of a person. He asked Nuru for help so later explorers would not lose everything they carried in their minds.

The Temple of Secrets

Anky said that secrets written in the Temple’s books would stay and help explorers resist further mental loss. What began as protection became an institution: notes, scrolls, collaborative theories, a communal equipment pool, and a record for whoever came next.

He opposed hoarding useful information. When Cerwin could not contribute an item in exchange for a Wand of Magic Missiles, Anky gave him his own Golden Boar Ring so the communal system could remain reciprocal without denying help. “It’s me job! Me duty as a sharing knight!!”

What Anky reported

On 6 March, Anky said Nuru told him Voraketh was Physisia’s favorite island and confirmed that Talan made the Chains and their guardians. He also relayed Physisia’s message through Pappy: the Chains were good at first but had become a curse. Anky did not leap from that evidence to destruction. He wanted to learn what the Chains held back before deciding what should happen.

Wisdom without pretending certainty

Anky’s occasional wisdom and his comedy grow from the same habit: he is comfortable admitting that he does not fully understand the world. In February 2025, a spiritual encounter connected to Cala leaves him with answers to questions he did not know and no answers to the questions he did. His conclusion is not polished enlightenment. He found enough of himself inside himself to know why he is who he is—and that is enough to continue.

The scene remains physically and unmistakably Anky: he guards a tight “hobo pile” of his belongings, gives a thumbs-up, and vomits into a bucket. Growth integrates with the person he already is rather than replacing him with a solemn prophet.

Small moments of practical caution

Anky’s judgment is visible well before the Chains become the central mystery. During a snowy descent in January 2025, he recognizes that control is already gone, tries to remain upright, and rides out the resulting chaos without pretending dignity will stop it. In June, approaching people known for strict rules, he warns that bringing Eugene inside may be unwise. He does not need to master a culture before respecting the possibility that its boundaries have consequences.

These smaller scenes clarify the method behind his later question about the Chains. Uncertainty does not paralyze Anky, and it does not authorize him to act as if he understands more than he does. He adjusts, remembers what the situation has shown him, and tries not to make an irreversible choice merely to feel decisive.

Map, scrolls, and shared research

By 21 March, Anky had an angel make a map of Voraketh, placed scrolls at the Temple, and encouraged others to theorize together and build a plan for surviving and eventually leaving. By 29 March, he openly said the island was making him lose things and that its excessive order disturbed him.

He wanted to leave. He stayed because Nuru had asked him, according to Anky, for a full report. His explanation was simple: “Me is a gnome of my word!”

20 April 2026 · the final expedition

Anky abandons the proposed northern boat journey and instead travels with Alfred Riverheart and Cerwin Rayolet to seek motes. When the portal closes behind them, he says they are two hours from the Chains. That distance is his estimate, not a measured map coordinate.

An earlier hostile encounter forces a retreat. Anky teleports himself and Alfred away and calls for Cerwin to run. The construct waiting nearer the Chains is a separate encounter; its identity must not be merged with that first creature.

Approaching the Chains, Anky and Alfred try to get past the construct. During the fight Anky repeatedly urges Alfred to flee; Alfred refuses to leave him. The explicit 20 April narration says the construct kills both in its grip. The Writer then records it carrying their bodies to the chain’s edge, throwing them across and returning to its watch.

Anky’s final prayer is posted after the death narration and expresses regret that he has failed. The posting interval does not establish an in-world duration for the dying. The following day’s narration confirms that Cerwin witnessed the two being killed and discarded. Cerwin then falls during his own attempted escape; his later appearance with Anky in the afterlife is another stage of the account.

The recovered scene fixes the earlier gap in Anky’s death record. It does not establish that a later resurrection was impossible or that every construct at the Chains behaves identically.

The records remain

Anky’s importance is not that he was destined to die. Voraketh took something from him; he built a place where knowledge could survive; he shared rather than hoarded; he remained from duty despite wanting to leave; and after his death, later explorers inherited an evidence base instead of beginning alone.

His lasting method is a question rather than a doctrine: if nobody knows what a system is doing, learn before destroying it. That humility makes him useful in a world where ancient structures may be prisons, protections, curses, or all three at once.

Anky should not be mistaken for a fool who secretly possesses every answer. Scribonia seeks a system’s logic, Elenia gives experience religious and moral meaning, and Arjahn expects a comprehensible structure from divine authority. Anky’s distinct strength is narrower and rarer: he can remain functional while the answer is still missing, and he notices when everyone else is disguising that same ignorance as certainty.

Record boundary: the April 20 expedition and deaths of Anky and Alfred, Cerwin’s death on April 21 and the later afterlife appearances are established. The fatal encounter is now recovered from the Wasteland scene: the chain-guard construct kills Anky and Alfred on 20 April.

The island seen through a tree

At the Last Grove, Anky discovers invisible writing, studies ancient magic resembling Druid Grove and receives a vision of the ordered forest, Chains and disappearing inner land. It gives his mapmaking a vital starting point, without revealing the central threat’s identity.

A title he can question

In the February 2025 inquiry Anky introduces himself as formerly of the saint variety. He seeks a drink said to help a person discover himself, and the experience leaves him with answers to questions he did not know and gaps in those he did. His uncertainty is his own experience, not an objective judgment about his mental ability.

This questioning does not erase the later observed recognition by Nuru, his peace-making or the work of the sharing knight. A person’s earlier doubt and later responsibility can remain true together. Unidentified voices and private revelations are not given an authoritative explanation here.

October 2025 · food promised to others

As another journey approaches, Anky asks whether they can stop in town for fresh food because he has promised it. He asks where the journey will take them and whether they are passing through the Roads or staying. The excitement is accompanied by an admission that he is not well prepared.

Care takes a concrete form: people elsewhere are expecting food. His curiosity belongs to a traveler with commitments, humor and appetites, rather than a figure whose only purpose is to deliver hidden knowledge.

These earlier scenes remain beside his Voraketh work, map, Temple of Secrets, sharing practices and final recovered expedition. The established death and afterlife records remain intact; the fatal encounter is now recovered from the separate Wasteland channel.

Recorded scenes

Dates refer to transcript postings, not an independently established in-world calendar.

  • 18 February 2025 · questioning the title
  • Answers and unanswered questions
  • His account of finding himself
  • 13 October · promised fresh food
  • Asking about the journey

Before the Temple · notes for whoever came next

Anky’s location notes show him trying to understand Voraketh in October and November 2025. He combines encounters with Murr, constructs and an unnaturally ordered landscape with unstable theories about rebirth, mechanical land and consuming hunger. His tree-touch vision does not independently confirm the explanations he builds around it.

His November note is left in a tree marked with a red ribbon. This small act of sharing precedes the later Temple of Secrets: he already wants other travelers to inherit what he has learned, including uncertainty. Neither the early note nor its vision replaces the later map or changes his established death and the now recovered fatal expedition.

Scenes in sequence

Selected scenes keep the knowledge available at each stage distinct from later discoveries. Dates identify source postings in UTC.

  1. 2026-04-20 · checked scenes

    Retreat from the first creature

    Anky teleports himself and Alfred away and urges Cerwin to run after their portal has closed.

    Known at this stage
    He regards the earlier hostile encounter as beyond their preparation.
    Consequence
    The retreat brings them toward the Chains and a different waiting construct.
    Still unresolved
    His two-hour estimate does not fix map geometry.

    Receipt 1 · Receipt 2

  2. 2026-04-20 → 2026-04-21 · checked scenes

    The construct kills Anky and Alfred

    Anky urges Alfred to flee; Alfred refuses to leave him. Explicit narration then records the construct killing both and discarding their bodies across the Chains.

    Known at this stage
    The attempt to return has become a fight for escape.
    Consequence
    The recovered 20 April killing scene explains Anky’s later afterlife appearance; Cerwin falls the following day.
    Still unresolved
    This death scene does not prove that no later resurrection could occur.

    Receipt 1 · Receipt 2 · Receipt 3 · Receipt 4 · Receipt 5

brief.status: Killed with Alfred by a construct at the Binding Chains on 20 April 2026; later appears in the afterlife.
brief.basis: Existing public dossier, explicit status facts and named timeline participants. Selected events are a reading guide, not a complete list or a ranking of importance.

profile.personality: Anky is frightened, disordered, generous, and unusually comfortable admitting that he does not understand. His comedy and wisdom share that humility: he can guard a hobo pile, vomit after revelation, and still ask the question everyone else skipped—what do the Chains hold before anyone breaks more of them?
profile.achievements: A traveler and sharing knight who carries uncertainty, humor and practical care into the institutions he leaves behind.
profile.relationships: Nuru publicly recognizes Anky’s service, but Anky’s holiness is expressed most clearly through mortal sharing. Cerwin receives help even without an item to exchange and later reaches Anky on the road to the afterlife; Alfred joins the last known journey; Coralyn, Carmen, Sildithas, Brianna, and Ghilsen share the Shadow Roads history. His community inherits records instead of only grief.

sourceReview.scope: Selected return, leadership and death-scene corrections. Original archives remain external; explicit canon clarification is distinguished from recollection.
